screening_rule: Include work only when its empirical unit, outcome, evidence surface, or infrastructure mechanism helps delimit upstream/downstream package identity, build-time testing, official build records, or artifact reproducibility. Keyword overlap alone is insufficient.

official_mechanism_sources.title: autopkgtest(1)
official_mechanism_sources.use: Distinguishes as-installed binary-package tests from build-time test execution.

excluded_examples.reason: Hosted project CI differs in ownership, recipe surface, package lineage, and official distribution-build identity.
They study rebuilt artifact equality or source differences, not whether official production records retain positive test-execution evidence.
As-installed package testing is a different lifecycle stage from tests executed during source-package builds.

novelty_assessment.warranted_claim: To our knowledge, prior work has examined package matching and evolution across Linux distributions, package test suites, historical testability, package reconstruction and reproducibility, and build-log-supported package diagnosis separately. We found no directly equivalent empirical design that jointly relates upstream executable test capability, downstream package-level testing intent, and positive test-execution evidence preserved in official distribution build records for matched packages across independent distribution families.
superseded_blockers: Web of Science and Scopus searches and exports require unavailable institutional access.
Consensus and Scite were unavailable, so Smart Citation and correction/retraction checks were not completed through those services.
The accessible search is not a systematic-review-grade guarantee of completeness.
novelty_assessment.supersession_note: The first two historical access conditions are not scientific gates under the 2026-08-13 author amendment. The final statement remains a scope limitation: this paper does not claim systematic or exhaustive literature coverage.
